title: AnomalyEvent
description: One line of data/anomalies.jsonl: a disagreement or contradiction between sources that the merge detected and did NOT resolve by overwriting. Today merge_partial computes these (MergeResult.anomalies) and every collector discards them; this ledger is where they go instead. Append-only.

source.description: The source whose observation triggered the anomaly.

kind.description: disagreement = a lower-precedence, non-empty, different value was dropped (merge rule 3/5/6); created_at_disagreement = rule 4, more than 2 s apart; inverted_bounds = rule 8; resurrected = rule 7; parse_partial = a page parsed but one card failed (collector counted it in errors); other_account = a trumpstruth entry not authored by realDonaldTrump was skipped; yield_below_min = a page returned fewer items than min_yield.

field.description: Record field for disagreement kinds; null otherwise.

kept.description: Rendered value kept, as '<source>=<value>' truncated to 200 chars.

dropped.description: Rendered value dropped, as '<source>=<value>' truncated to 200 chars.

detail.description: The legacy one-line string (e.g. kind_disagreement:<ts_id>:api=original,cnn=reblog) so grep on old formats still works.

url.description: The page or API URL that produced the observation, when known; lets explain <ts_id> point at the evidence.

x-queries: count by kind per day: a jump in created_at_disagreement usually means a source changed its timezone rendering
resurrected: every one is a possible false deletion; each should become a lesson or a confirmed source quirk
disagreement where field=kind and dropped starts with cnn=: expected background (cnn cannot see quotes or replies)
